prompt:
Produce up to 8 distinct, useful design or engineering actions for the task below. Explore materially different mechanisms, including non-obvious alternatives. Respect every constraint. Give executable changes in the target domain, with an implementation step and a falsifiable check. Do not claim unmeasured gains, invent supporting facts, or rename the same action several ways. State actions in the user's terms; omit donor names and analogy explanations from the answer. Fewer actions, including none, are acceptable when no additional valid action remains. Keep each action compact: aim for 60–80 words TOTAL across its five fields, never more than 110. Suggested field budgets: action 8 words, mechanism 16, implementation 22, check 20, risk 10. The 110-word maximum applies to the SUM of all five values, not to each field.

Task:
{
  "title": "Offline notes merge without losing authorship",
  "brief": "A two-device note application permits offline edits to paragraphs for up to 48 hours. Both devices may alter the same paragraph, reorder paragraphs, and reconnect in either order. The existing merge replaces the older complete document.",
  "constraints": [
    "Every paragraph has a stable ID, and each edit has an author/device ID and logical revision.",
    "Keep the original text of conflicting edits until a user resolves them.",
    "No external synchronization service can be added.",
    "A note contains at most 500 paragraphs; individual paragraphs are at most 8 KB."
  ],
  "success_criteria": [
    "Independent paragraph edits survive either reconnect order.",
    "A conflict remains explainable to the user.",
    "Describe a deterministic replay test including a deletion versus an edit."
  ],
  "non_goals": [
    "Requiring constant connectivity or automatically deciding whose prose is better."
  ]
}
Return JSON only: {"actions":[{"action":"...","mechanism":"...","implementation":"...","check":"...","risk":"..."}],"abstention_reason":""}. Use abstention_reason only to explain an empty action list. No tools or additional research.
